newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio de Janeiro signs 11.6 bln reais debt rollover.
newsitem.headline: Rio de Janeiro signs 11.6 bln reais debt rollover.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state has signed an accord with the Brazilian government to roll over 11.6 billion reais in state debt over 30 years, state officials said in a statement.
The deal, reached last week, calls for the rescheduling of 5.25 billion reais in state debt and a 3.4 billion-real shortfall left by failed state bank Banerj, the statement said.

The agreement, signed by state Governor Marcello Alencar and Finance Minister Pedro Malan, also calls for Brasilia to lend the state 2.95 billion reais to restructure the state's financing system, it said.
The accord allows the state to repay the debt over 30 years at a 7.5 percent annual interest rate plus inflation as calculated by the IGP-DI index, the statement said.

The federal government is charging Rio more than the six percent it charged Sao Paulo, Minas Gerais and Rio Grande do Sul states because Rio could only offer 10 percent of its total debt as a financial guarantee, it said.
If it raises that to the 20 percent offered by other states, the interest rate will fall to six percent, the rate being paid by Sao Paulo, Minas and Rio GRande do Sul, it added.
